artifact.canonical_name: Negotiating strict latency limits for dynamic real-time services in vehicular time-sensitive networks
artifact.organization: TU Dresden / HAW Hamburg / TU Eindhoven

sources.title: Negotiating strict latency limits for dynamic real-time services in vehicular time-sensitive networks
sources.role: Author arXiv paper/preprint used to verify the architecture, evaluation scope, material claims, and limitations available in the primary text.

claims.text: The authors propose a service-discovery/QoS negotiation mechanism that communicates application requirements to a central TSN controller, which performs admission/resource configuration using network-calculus delay budgets.

In the evaluated realistic IVN, the authors find the per-queue delay-budget/network-calculus reservation approach to be the only tested scheme that consistently enforces hard latency constraints; alternative interval-based approaches can misconfigure resources.
Real-time data transfer bypasses the controller after flows/reservations are established, while the controller remains a setup-time dependency and potential single point of failure.

metrics.name: setup/signaling duration with SOME/IP scatter
metrics.context: 450 subscriptions in the realistic-IVN simulation; negotiation without scatter is reported around 2 ms.

metrics.name: target worst-case end-to-end latency per flow
metrics.context: Critical-flow deadline used in the IVN evaluation.

metrics.name: maximum relative idle-slope provisioning versus flow-interval baseline
metrics.context: Delay-budget approach may provision up to roughly three times higher idle slope to guarantee deadlines.

limitations.text: The central controller is a potential single point of failure during reservation/setup, although established real-time data paths do not continuously depend on it.
Hard deadline guarantees can require substantial bandwidth overprovisioning relative to less conservative schemes.
Reliable delivery/retransmission is treated as orthogonal to the strict real-time reservation problem, and redundancy mechanisms such as FRER are left for extensions.

targets.target: Verify the architecture, evaluation setup, material claims and limitations reported for Negotiating strict latency limits for dynamic real-time services in vehicular time-sensitive networks; preserve paper results as AUTHOR_CLAIM unless independently established.
targets.finding: The full v3 primary text verifies the SOA-to-TSN signaling architecture, network-calculus delay-budget method, 450-subscription/11.1-ms result, 1-ms deadline target, overprovisioning trade-off, controller/SPOF and reliability limitations.

editorial.why_now_note: Dynamic service deployment makes deterministic network configuration a runtime control-plane responsibility rather than a static communication-matrix-only activity.
editorial.rationale: Directly connects application/SOA QoS requests to centralized TSN resource control with worst-case latency validation; one of the strongest network-control architecture items in the intake.
